# Terraform AWS Backup Management Module

 [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management/commits)


Terraform module to create and manage AWS Backup resources at scale: backup vaults (including logically air-gapped
vaults), backup plans and selections, advanced backup options per resource type, and AWS Backup Region Settings.
It helps standardize backup strategies, enforce encryption with KMS (including automatic key creation with
always-on rotation), and streamline operations across environments and accounts.


---

## Introduction

This module provisions and manages AWS Backup across your AWS accounts and regions.

It supports:

- Backup vault creation with optional KMS encryption, or a logically air-gapped vault.
- KMS key management through the `vault.encryption` block: create a new key, bring your own key ARN, or
  reference an existing key by alias. Key rotation is always enabled; the rotation period defaults to
  90 days and is configurable between 90 and 2560 days.
- Backup plans with rules, retention lifecycles, and cross-region/cross-vault copy actions.
- Backup selections by tag, by explicit ARN, and by condition expressions.
- A module-managed IAM backup service role, created automatically when the module owns the vault.
- Advanced backup options per resource type (e.g. Windows VSS) and AWS Backup Region Settings opt-ins.

## Resource naming

Names are derived from the organization and spoke values supplied by the Terragrunt hierarchy:

| Resource        | Name pattern                                  |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Backup vault    | `<vault.name>` or `<vault.name_prefix>-<system>-vault` |
| KMS alias       | `alias/<vault name>`                          |
| Backup plan     | `<plan_key>-<system>-plan`                    |
| Backup rule     | `<plan_key>-<rule_key>-rule`                  |
| Backup selection| `<plan_key>-<resource_key>-selection`         |
| IAM role        | `<vault name>-service-role`                   |

Where `<system>` is a short slug built from the organization unit, environment name, environment type,
spoke identifier, and region.

## Reserved inputs

The `ram` and `legal_holds` variables are accepted by the module and validated as part of its interface,
but no `aws_ram_*` or `aws_backup_legal_hold` resources are provisioned yet. Set them only to pin the
intended configuration ahead of a future release.

## Known limitations

- Backup selections currently resolve their IAM role only from the module-managed backup service role.
  Running with `vault.create = false` together with `backup_plans.<plan>.resources` does not pick up the
  per-plan `role_arn` and will fail during plan. Until this is addressed, use `vault.create = true`, or
  omit `resources` and manage the selections outside this module.

## Usage


**IMPORTANT:** The `master` branch is used in `source` just as an example. In your code, do not pin to `master` because there may be breaking changes between releases.
Instead pin to the release tag (e.g. `?ref=vX.Y.Z`) of one of our [latest releases](https://github.com/terraform-module-aws-backup-management/releases).


This module is consumed through Terragrunt. The recommended way to bootstrap a deployment is the
built-in `terragrunt scaffold` command, which sources `.boilerplate/boilerplate.yml` from this repository
and generates `terragrunt.hcl`, `inputs.yaml`, and `local-tags.json` in the target directory.

### 1. Scaffold the deployment

```sh
# Create and enter the target deployment directory
mkdir -p production/us-east-1/001/backup-management
cd production/us-east-1/001/backup-management

# Scaffold the module (do NOT use --working-dir)
terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management

# Edit inputs.yaml with deployment-specific values
vi inputs.yaml

# Apply
terragrunt apply
```

### 2. Fill in `inputs.yaml`

Scaffold pre-populates `inputs.yaml` with every module variable, already annotated with
`(Required)`/`(Optional)` markers and defaults. Variables supplied by the Terragrunt hierarchy —
`is_hub`, `spoke_def`, `org`, and `extra_tags` — are not part of this file.

```yaml
# Module configuration

# vault: # (Optional) Backup vault configuration. Default: {create: false, name: "", name_prefix: "", force_destroy: false}
vault:
  create: true            # (Optional) Create the backup vault with this module. Default: true
  name: ""                # (Optional) Explicit vault name. Required when name_prefix is empty. Mutually exclusive with name_prefix. Default: ""
  name_prefix: "acme-prod" # (Optional) Prefix used to build the name as "<prefix>-<system_name_short>-vault". Required when name is empty. Default: ""
  force_destroy: false    # (Optional) Allow vault deletion even if it still holds recovery points. Default: false
  encryption:             # (Optional) Preferred encryption block. Takes precedence over the deprecated flat fields. Default: null
    create: false         # (Optional) Create a new KMS key and alias for this vault. Default: false
    key: ""               # (Optional) Existing KMS Key ARN. Used when create=false. Default: ""
    alias: ""             # (Optional) Existing KMS Alias, format "alias/<name>". Used when key is empty and create=false. Default: ""
    deletion_window: 30   # (Optional) KMS key deletion window in days. Valid: 7-30. Default: 30
    key_description: ""   # (Optional) Description for the created KMS key. Default: "" (auto-generated)
    rotation_period: 90   # (Optional) KMS key rotation period in days. Valid: 90-2560. Default: 90. Rotation is always enabled
  # DEPRECATED flat encryption fields — only read when vault.encryption is omitted
  # encryption_create_key: false # DEPRECATED (Optional) Use vault.encryption.create instead. Default: null
  # encryption_key: ""           # DEPRECATED (Optional) Use vault.encryption.key instead. Default: ""
  # encryption_alias: ""         # DEPRECATED (Optional) Use vault.encryption.alias instead. Default: ""

# air_gapped: # (Optional) Logically air-gapped vault settings; replaces the standard vault when enabled
air_gapped:
  enabled: false          # (Optional) Create a logically air-gapped backup vault instead of a standard vault. Default: false
  min_retention_days: 0   # (Optional) Minimum retention in days for recovery points in the air-gapped vault. Default: 0
  max_retention_days: 0   # (Optional) Maximum retention in days for recovery points in the air-gapped vault. Default: 0

# region_settings: # (Required) AWS Backup Region Settings. The variable has no default, so the key must be present
region_settings:
  enabled: false          # (Optional) Apply AWS Backup region settings in this region. Default: false
  opt_ins: {}             # (Optional) Map of resource type => ENABLED|DISABLED. Default: {}
  management_preference: {} # (Optional) Map of resource type => SYSTEM|USER. Default: {}

# backup_plans: # (Optional) Map of backup plans to create, keyed by plan name. Default: {} (no plans created)
backup_plans: {}

# ram: # (Optional) Cross-account vault sharing. RESERVED — accepted but not provisioned yet
ram:
  enabled: false          # (Optional) Reserved for AWS RAM sharing of the vault. Default: false
  accounts: []            # (Optional) AWS account IDs to share the vault with. Default: []

# legal_holds: # (Optional) Legal holds. RESERVED — accepted but not provisioned yet. Default: {}
legal_holds: {}
```

A populated `backup_plans` entry looks like this:

```yaml
backup_plans:
  primary:                                    # Plan name fragment; final name is "primary-<system>-plan"
    # role_arn: "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/BackupServiceRole"
    #                                         # (Optional) Only consulted when vault.create=false
    rules:                                    # (Required) Map of backup rules, keyed by rule name
      daily:
        # target_vault_name: "existing-vault" # (Required when vault.create=false) Pre-existing target vault
        schedule: "cron(0 12 * * ? *)"        # (Optional) CRON or rate expression. Default: null
        timezone: "UTC"                       # (Optional) IANA timezone for the schedule. Default: null (UTC)
        continuous_backup: true               # (Optional) Enable point-in-time backup. Default: false
        start_window: 60                      # (Optional) Minutes to start the job. Default: null (AWS default 60)
        completion_window: 180                # (Optional) Minutes to complete the job. Default: null (AWS default 180)
        recovery_point_tags:                  # (Optional) Tags applied to created recovery points. Default: null
          Purpose: "daily"
        lifecycle:                            # (Optional) Retention lifecycle. Default: omitted
          cold_storage_after: 30              # (Optional) Days before moving to cold storage
          delete_after: 365                   # (Optional) Days before deletion; at least cold_storage_after + 90
          opt_in: true                        # (Optional) Archive for supported resources
        copy_action:                          # (Optional) Copy recovery points to another vault. Default: omitted
          destination_vault_arn: "arn:aws:backup:us-west-2:111122223333:backup-vault:dr"
          lifecycle:
            cold_storage_after: 30
            delete_after: 730
            opt_in: true
    advanced:                                 # (Optional) Advanced backup settings. Default: omitted
      resource_type: "EC2"                    # (Optional) AWS currently supports only "EC2"
      backup_options:
        WindowsVSS: "enabled"                 # Valid: enabled|disabled
    resources:                                # (Optional) Backup selections, keyed by selection name
      by_tag:
        tags:                                 # (Optional) Select resources by tag. Default: []
          - type: "STRINGEQUALS"              # (Required) Match type. Valid: STRINGEQUALS
            key: "backup"                     # (Required) Tag key
            value: "true"                     # (Required) Tag value
      explicit:
        include_arns:                         # (Optional) Explicit ARNs to include. Default: []
          - "arn:aws:ec2:us-east-1:111122223333:volume/vol-abc"
        exclude_arns: []                      # (Optional) Explicit ARNs to exclude. Default: []
        conditions:                           # (Optional) Condition expressions. Default: []
          - string_equals:
              key: "aws:ResourceTag/Env"
              value: "prod"
          - string_like:
              key: "aws:ResourceTag/App"
              value: "*api*"
```

### 3. The generated `terragrunt.hcl`

Scaffold renders the file below — there is no need to hand-author it. Note how `inputs.yaml` is loaded
as `local.local_vars` and wired into the `inputs` block, while `org`, `spoke_def`, and `extra_tags` come
from the parent hierarchy.

```hcl
locals {
  local_vars  = yamldecode(file("./inputs.yaml"))
  spoke_vars  = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("spoke-inputs.yaml")))
  region_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("region-inputs.yaml")))
  env_vars    = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-inputs.yaml")))
  global_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-inputs.yaml")))

  local_tags  = jsondecode(file("./local-tags.json"))
  spoke_tags  = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("spoke-tags.json")))
  region_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("region-tags.json")))
  env_tags    = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("env-tags.json")))
  global_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-tags.json")))

  tags = merge(
    local.global_tags,
    local.env_tags,
    local.region_tags,
    local.spoke_tags,
    local.local_tags
  )
}

include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}

terraform {
  source = "git::https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management.git?ref=v1.2.5"
}

inputs = {
  is_hub          = false
  org             = local.env_vars.org
  spoke_def       = local.spoke_vars.spoke
  region_settings = local.local_vars.region_settings
  vault           = try(local.local_vars.vault, {})
  air_gapped      = try(local.local_vars.air_gapped, {})
  backup_plans    = try(local.local_vars.backup_plans, {})
  ram             = try(local.local_vars.ram, {})
  legal_holds     = try(local.local_vars.legal_holds, {})
  extra_tags      = local.tags
}
```

## Quick Start

1. Install Terragrunt and OpenTofu/Terraform, and configure AWS credentials (for example via AWS SSO).
2. Create the deployment directory and run
   `terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-backup-management` inside it.
3. Edit the generated `inputs.yaml`. At minimum set `vault.name_prefix` (or `vault.name`) and add at
   least one entry under `backup_plans`.
4. Run `terragrunt init` to initialize the module.
5. Run `terragrunt plan` to review the changes, then `terragrunt apply` to provision AWS Backup.
6. Verify the resulting vault, plans, and selections in the AWS Backup console.


## Examples

All examples below show the `inputs.yaml` produced by `terragrunt scaffold`; `terragrunt.hcl` is left as
generated.

## Minimal — vault plus a daily plan

```yaml
# inputs.yaml
vault:
  create: true
  name_prefix: "acme-dev"

region_settings:
  enabled: false

backup_plans:
  default:
    rules:
      daily:
        schedule: "cron(0 2 * * ? *)"
        timezone: "UTC"
        continuous_backup: true
    resources:
      by_tag:
        tags:
          - type: "STRINGEQUALS"
            key: "backup"
            value: "true"
```

Creates an unencrypted vault, a daily plan with point-in-time recovery, a module-managed backup service
role, and a tag-based selection.

## Encrypted vault with a module-managed KMS key

```yaml
# inputs.yaml
vault:
  create: true
  name_prefix: "acme-prod"
  force_destroy: false
  encryption:
    create: true          # Module creates the KMS key and alias/<vault name>
    deletion_window: 30
    rotation_period: 90   # Rotation is always enabled

region_settings:
  enabled: true
  opt_ins:
    DynamoDB: "ENABLED"
    EBS: "ENABLED"

backup_plans:
  critical:
    rules:
      monthly:
        schedule: "cron(0 0 1 * ? *)"
        timezone: "UTC"
        lifecycle:
          cold_storage_after: 30
          delete_after: 365
        copy_action:
          destination_vault_arn: "arn:aws:backup:us-west-2:111122223333:backup-vault:dr"
          lifecycle:
            cold_storage_after: 60
            delete_after: 730
    advanced:
      resource_type: "EC2"
      backup_options:
        WindowsVSS: "enabled"
    resources:
      tag_sel:
        tags:
          - type: "STRINGEQUALS"
            key: "backup"
            value: "true"
```

Creates a KMS-encrypted vault, enables region opt-ins, and configures monthly backups with a cross-region
copy and Windows VSS support.

## Bring your own KMS key

```yaml
# inputs.yaml
vault:
  create: true
  name_prefix: "acme-prod"
  encryption:
    create: false
    key: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab"

region_settings:
  enabled: false

backup_plans: {}
```

Reference an existing key by alias instead by leaving `key` empty and setting
`alias: "alias/my-backup-key"`.

## Logically air-gapped vault

```yaml
# inputs.yaml
vault:
  create: true
  name_prefix: "acme-vault"

air_gapped:
  enabled: true
  min_retention_days: 30
  max_retention_days: 3650

region_settings:
  enabled: false

backup_plans:
  immutable:
    rules:
      weekly:
        schedule: "cron(0 3 ? * SUN *)"
        timezone: "UTC"
        lifecycle:
          delete_after: 365
```

Logically air-gapped vaults are always managed by an AWS-owned key, so the `vault.encryption` settings do
not apply to them.

## Attaching plans to an existing vault

> **Note:** see *Known limitations* — combining `vault.create: false` with a `resources` block is not
> functional yet, because the per-plan `role_arn` is not resolved for selections.

```yaml
# inputs.yaml
vault:
  create: false           # The module does not create the vault or the IAM role

region_settings:
  enabled: false

backup_plans:
  shared:
    role_arn: "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/BackupServiceRole"  # Required when vault.create=false
    rules:
      daily:
        target_vault_name: "central-backup-vault"                 # Required when vault.create=false
        schedule: "cron(0 5 * * ? *)"
        timezone: "UTC"
        lifecycle:
          delete_after: 90
    resources:
      by_tag:
        tags:
          - type: "STRINGEQUALS"
            key: "backup"
            value: "true"
```
